Fibroadenoma is generally an oval mass with sharp margins, often T2 hyperintense, with non-enhancing internal septa and progressive enhancement (type I). The curve alone is not enough: morphology (shape, margins, internal enhancement) and kinetics are read together, and in high-risk women a new lesion, even if benign-appearing, should be compared with previous exams.
